rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet kept asking Gabriel for additional recitation modes after first receiving one, until they reached seven.
rows.anchor: أن ابن عباس حدثه أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال أقرأني جبريل على حرف

rows.speaker: ابن شهاب
rows.claim: Ibn Shihab says the seven ahruf concern a single matter whose forms do not differ over what is lawful or forbidden.
rows.anchor: قال ابن شهاب بلغني أن تلك السبعة الأحرف إنما هي في الأمر الذي يكون واحدا

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Umm Ayyub reports the Prophet's teaching that the Quran was revealed in seven ahruf and whichever form one recites is correct; the source repeats it with variant wording.
rows.anchor: أن أم أيوب أخبرته أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال أنزل القرآن على سبعة أحرف أيها قرأت أصبت

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Sulayman ibn Surad reports a prophetic account in which two angels offer one mode of recitation, and one keeps granting increases until seven.
rows.anchor: عن سليمان بن صرد يرفعه قال أتاني ملكان فقال أحدهما اقرأ قال على كم قال على حرف

rows.speaker: شقيق
rows.claim: Shuqayq recounts Ibn Abbas preaching and explaining Surat al-Nur from the pulpit, adding that the Romans would have become Muslim had they heard him.
rows.anchor: عن شقيق قال شهدت ابن عباس وولي الموسم فقرأ سورة النور على المنبر وفسرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabari cites God's commands to reflect on Quranic verses and take heed from their examples, arguing that these commands presuppose comprehension of accessible meanings.
rows.anchor: كتاب أنزلناه إليك مبارك ليدبروا آياته وليتذكر أولو الألباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He argues it is absurd to command people who do not understand Arabic to learn from an Arabic poem; they must first understand its language, then reflect.
rows.anchor: محال أن يقال لبعض أصناف الأمم الذين لا يعقلون كلام العرب ولا يفهمونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Therefore, those who know Arabic can understand verses whose interpretation God has not reserved; this defeats rejection of commentators' explanations of accessible verses.
rows.anchor: فسد قول من أنكر تفسير المفسرين من كتاب الله وتنزيله ما لم يحجب عن خلقه تأويله

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: Ibn Masud recounts two differing claims about a surah's recitation; a man urges them to read as taught and warns that earlier peoples were destroyed by disputing with their prophets.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله قال اختلف رجلان في سورة فقال هذا أقرأني النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reports that his group disputed whether a surah had thirty-five or thirty-six verses; the Prophet condemned such disagreement and, through Ali, instructed them to read as taught.
rows.anchor: عن عاصم عن زر بن حبيش قال قال عبد الله بن مسعود تمارينا في سورة من القرآن

rows.speaker: زيد بن أرقم
rows.claim: Zayd ibn Arqam reports a question about differing recitations taught by Ibn Masud, Zayd and Ubayy; Ali answers that each may read as taught and all are good.
rows.anchor: عن زيد بن أرقم قال كنا معه في المسجد فحدثنا ساعة ثم قال جاء رجل إلى رسول الله

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: Umar recounts challenging Hisham's different recitation of Surat al-Furqan; the Prophet confirms both forms as revealed and says the Quran came in seven ahruf, so read what is easy.
rows.anchor: أخبراه أنهما سمعا عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه يقول سمعت هشام بن حكيم يقرأ سورة الفرقان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi says he heard Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm and transmitted from him; Abu Bakr al-Khwarizmi appointed him to teach his lesson during his absence.
rows.anchor: وسمع أبا العباس الأصم وروى عنه واستخلفه الأستاذ أبو بكر الخوارزمي على درسه عند غيبته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi notes that he wrote major works and critical supplements addressing leading scholars of language and grammar.
rows.anchor: وله المصنفات الكبار والاستدراكات على الفحول من علماء اللغة والنحو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He studied intensively with al-Thaʿlabi for years, visiting daily to hear, read, annotate, memorize, research and discuss while working through poetry collections and language books.
rows.anchor: كنت قد لازمته سنين أدخل عليه عند طلوع الشمس وأخرج لغروبها أسمع وأقرأ وأعلق وأحفظ وأبحث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Thaʿlabi urged him to devote himself to Quran commentary; al-Wahidi replied that literary study prepared him for tafsir and continued visiting until death separated them.
rows.anchor: إنك لم تبق ديوانا من الشعر إلا قضيت حقه أما آن لك أن تتفرغ لتفسير كتاب الله العزيز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As a young man he studied under Abu al-Hasan al-Darir, whom he describes as outstanding in subtle grammar and the intricacies of Arabic, and devoted to training him.
rows.anchor: أبي الحسن علي بن محمد بن إبراهيم الضرير رحمه الله وكان من أبرع أهل زمانه في لطائف النحو وغوامضه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Under al-Darir, al-Wahidi studied grammar, morphology and semantics, compiled nearly one hundred fascicles on difficult issues, heard works on grammar, metrics and linguistic causes, and received his book on Ibn Mihran's qiraat justifications.
rows.anchor: قرأت عليه جوامع النحو والتصريف والمعاني وعلقت عنه قريبا من مائة جزء في المسائل المشكلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He studied with Abu al-Hasan Imran al-Maghribi al-Maliki, whom he calls unmatched in i'rab, and says he absorbed the finest of his knowledge during his stay.
rows.anchor: الشيخ الإمام أبو الحسن عمران بن موسى المغربي المالكي وكان واحد عصره وباقعة دهره في علم النحو
